mark_breakdown.desc: Write final simplified answer with $+ c$

subparts.solution:
$\int (x\sqrt{x} - 5\cos x)\,dx = \int (x^{\frac{3}{2}} - 5\cos x)\,dx$
$= \frac{2}{5}x^{\frac{5}{2}} - 5\sin x + c$
$= \frac{2}{5}x^2\sqrt{x} - 5\sin x + c$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Convert radical expressions to index form: $x\sqrt{x} = x^1 \cdot x^{1/2} = x^{3/2}$, then apply $\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}$ and $\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Simplify into radical form with $+ c$

subparts.solution:
$\int \left(\sin x + \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}\right)dx = \int (\sin x + x^{-\frac{1}{3}})\,dx$
$= -\cos x + \frac{3}{2}x^{\frac{2}{3}} + c$
$= -\cos x + \frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{x^2} + c$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use negative and fractional powers: $\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}} = x^{-1/3}$. Use $\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x$ and the power rule.
step_by_step: Rewrite the integrand with rational exponents: $\sin x + x^{-1/3}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Writing $\int \sin x\,dx = \cos x$ instead of $-\cos x$.
